en: Now, the characteristics of the colors of the limbs of this Śiva are described;
by knowing which, one whose bonds of māyā and the like have been burnt attains the state of Śiva. || 1 ||
Having drawn a wheel without the preceding [seed-syllables] and devoid of the four enclosures,
one should place the supreme syllable at its base.

The ritual deposition (nyāsa) according to the sequence of Śiva’s extraction, through the systematic unfolding of the mantras, is proclaimed as extending from Sarvātma-Śiva at the beginning up to Netra at the end. 3.
Oṃkāra, yavau, śiva, te, śubhāḥ, and again śa;
phadyava, and likewise bhūyas, bhūyas, and the words tathā. (4)
In the *śānti* [section], there are *sakasā*, *bhūyaḥ*, *vaśvajā*, and *visargaka*; then *bandharī*, followed by *svāhā*, *ṭa*, and *paś* at the very end. 5.
Then *rvā-ra*, *rvā-ra*, and likewise *e-ra-ha*; in the *śi-su* [section], the second syllable is long;
then *ghū-kā-ra*, *ra-kā-ra*, *hy-akā-ra*, and *pra-civa*. (6)
The letters *tm*, *kau*, *kāva*, *rvaya*, and *rṇā*, then the letter *i* and the *praṇava*;
at the end, *cam*, *bhā*, and again *na ca rayya*, and likewise *ntra hi ghū*. 7.
Then *pra*, *śca*, likewise *ṭa* and *he*, and further *bhūyaḥ* and *anta* itself;
*va* and *pu* are joined with *pra* by means of *visarga*, while *ma* is joined with *kāra* by means of *pi*. || 8 ||
Mount the sixth path; Rā, Ru, Śa, Śi, Pa, Ṭa, Ka, Ri; then Ra, Hau, and Ha; Ya, Ku, Ma, Va, Śa; and again Rā, Pu, Na. 9.

In the ninth path, there are *la*, *ṅka*, *ra*, *spṛ*, *ka*, *de*, *kā*, *rā*, *pa*, *ru*, *nā*, *na*, *va*, *sya*, *ji*, *mā*, *ka*, *ma*, *rā*, *śca*, *e*, *va*, *bha*, *śca*, *vā*, and finally *ca*. (10)
Rasa-sāha, Tamha, Ca-kinu-gho-vāś-ca, Ya-stataḥ, Meghadād-a-dvitīyāś-ca, Kasū-prāś-ca, Ramau, and Dhīḥ. || 11 ||
Sva-sau-śi-ya-pa-vā-kṣma-ś-ca, vi-dho-vā-ś-ca-ma-e-va-ca, ra-dya-va-jvā-rtavā-ssū-my-a, ramā-ś-ca-e-va-tata-ś-ca-hi. (12)
The *pabhapra* and *liyya* syllables, the fourteen *śikṣmāś* and *sataghātā*s, as well as the *rāvasānī* and *mavāpā*s, arise from the pause (*virāma*) between *r*, *va*, *ta*, *n*, and *u*. 13.
Yahannā, stvā, ca, hā, jñau, ca, hadatāyaḥ, śireva, ca, yokāraḥ, ca, vanau, hā, ca, ghoyādhaṣṭāḥ, ca, nuḥ, tataḥ. || 14 ||
Then follow gha, āvante, punaḥ, gāca, bha, śca, mo, ca, and from that, the syllable ta;
then ram, bharas, tam, rutāḥ, pra, śca, yavo, stuśi, ka, mā, and from that, sta. 15.
Likewise, there, the letters va, bha, pa, and ya follow at the end; then yo, ma, te, vā, va, ha, jñā, ya, ca, ha, ra, da, and again ta. (16)
Gapa, usmatmauca, vanda, śasta, bha, phaṭ, cuvāk, sañcasa, hā, kaṃpi, ya, and nibha—these likewise. || 17 ||
Cañca, ta, and likewise oṃkāra; bhavau and praṇava; magau, bavau, and likewise ya; ṭatmau and juṅkāra. || 18 ||
In the debate, he dispatched the son of Suhaḷandhra, named Sarvātmasaṃjña, along with the heart-mantra consisting of seventy syllables. || 19 ||
First, one should extract [the mantra] beginning with Oṃ and ending with Ha in due order;
from that, one should extract the eight-syllabled "Head" (Śiras), which is known as Suśiva.
Beyond that, one should place Jvālinī, the eleven-syllable Śikhā-mantra;
beyond that, the Piṅgala-mantra consisting of one hundred and six syllables.
Then, one should extract the Aghora-weapon mantra, characterized by thirty-two syllables,
followed by the twenty-four-syllable Gāyatrī of the Goddess in its proper sequence.
Therefore, the three-syllabled Netra is the supreme abode of all vidyās;

it should be known as consisting of two hundred and sixty-four syllables, established through the division of the heart and other limbs, bestowing both supernatural powers (siddhi) and liberation (mukti). 23.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, on the characteristics of the limbs of Śiva, in the Svāyambhuva-sūtra-saṅgraha.
